This chart shows official development assistance (ODA) as a share of gross national income for each DAC member.
ODA fell by 7.1% in 2024, the largest drop in a decade.
Debt service is principal repaid plus interest paid on external debt in the year shown.
Germany is now the second-largest donor, behind the United States.
Each bar splits debt service by creditor type: bilateral, multilateral and private.
Debt service payments have risen sharply since 2020 and are expected to keep climbing.
Donors report climate finance under their own methods, so the amount of private finance counted as mobilised differs between countries.
The latest data, for 2023, show climate finance at USD 115 billion.
Values are in constant US dollars, adjusted to a base year, so changes over time reflect volumes rather than price rises.
Only five donors currently meet the 0.7% target.

The UN target for ODA is 0.7% of gross national income.
Norway gives the most as a share of income.
The dotted line marks the 0.7% target.
Total ODA reached USD 223 billion in 2023.
Select a country to compare it with its income group.
Sub-Saharan Africa receives about a third of all bilateral ODA.
Hover over a segment to see its value.
Low-income countries now spend more on debt service than on health.
ODA counts grants in full and loans at their grant equivalent, under the method the DAC adopted in 2018.
China is the largest bilateral creditor to low-income countries.

In-donor refugee costs count as ODA when they cover a refugee's first year in the donor country.
In-donor refugee costs make up 14% of the total.
The table lists every country that reports to the International Debt Statistics.
Climate finance has doubled over the past decade.
Multilateral development banks lend on concessional terms to low-income countries and on market terms to middle-income countries.
The United Kingdom has cut its aid to 0.5% of gross national income.
The key number is the sum of all disbursements in the latest year the source reports.
Ukraine is the largest single recipient.
Commitments are what a donor promises; disbursements are what it pays out in the year.
External debt of low- and middle-income countries stands at USD 8.8 trillion.

A country's income group follows the World Bank's classification for the fiscal year of the data.
Interest payments are at a record high.
Figures before 2018 use the cash-flow method, so the line has a break at that year.
Most donors are below the target.
Shares are calculated from current prices, so they do not depend on the base year.
Health is the sector that receives the most ODA.
Use the filter above the chart to switch between commitments and disbursements.
The share going to least developed countries has fallen for three years in a row.
Under the Paris Agreement's new goal, developed countries are to lead in providing at least USD 300 billion a year in climate finance by 2035.
As of 2024, 34 countries are in or at high risk of debt distress.

Climate finance here covers mitigation, adaptation and projects that serve both.
Private creditors hold 40% of these countries' external debt.
Private finance mobilised is the private money that official interventions bring into a project.
Ethiopia receives more ODA than any other African country.
Darker shades mean a larger share of government revenue goes to external debt service.
The gap between commitments and disbursements has narrowed this year.
Data come from the OECD Creditor Reporting System, which records each aid project a donor reports.
Multilateral lending rose 12% last year.
A country appears in grey when its source reports no value for the year selected.
Sweden gives 0.9% of its national income.

The IMF's Special Drawing Rights are a reserve asset, so allocating them adds no debt service.
This is the highest level of climate finance on record.
Net flows are disbursements minus repayments, so they can be negative.
Debt service will peak in 2026.
Each dot is one country, placed by its income per person and its debt as a share of GDP.
The figure for 2024 is preliminary and may be revised.
Gross national income is the income a country's residents earn, at home and abroad.
Twelve countries spend more than a fifth of revenue on debt service.
The chart follows the latest data from the source, so its values change when the source publishes new figures.
Adaptation finance is still far below what countries need.

Bilateral ODA goes directly from a donor to a recipient; multilateral ODA passes through an organisation such as the World Bank.
Aid to Gaza has surged since October 2023.
Amounts are in billions of US dollars.
The United States provides about 30% of all DAC ODA.
The heat map orders recipients by the ODA they receive, with the largest at the top.
France has moved ahead of Japan in the donor ranking.
A projection is drawn as a dashed line, and reported years as a solid one.
Zambia is so far the only country to have finished a restructuring under the Common Framework.
The 0.15-0.20% target is the share of gross national income donors agreed to give to least developed countries.
Spending on education has stagnated since 2019.

A debt sustainability analysis judges whether a country can meet its debt payments without exceptional support.
The average interest rate on new loans is 5.2%.
Sort the table by any column to compare countries.
Kenya pays more to bondholders than to any other creditor.
Concessional loans carry interest rates below market rates and long grace periods.
Grants make up the bulk of ODA to fragile states this year.
The World Bank's International Development Association gives grants and low-interest loans to the poorest countries.
The total is down from USD 240 billion a year earlier.
This card counts a project once, under the sector its donor assigned it.
Mobilised private finance remains small, at under USD 20 billion.

Percentages may not add to 100 because of rounding.
Most of the increase comes from support to Ukraine.
Emergency response covers relief, food aid and short-term reconstruction after a crisis.
Net flows to Africa turned negative in 2023.
A country is in debt distress when it cannot meet its payments without restructuring.
Pakistan has the highest debt service of any lower-middle-income country.
Each line shows one donor's ODA as a share of its gross national income over time.
The figures show donors falling further behind their pledges.
Imputed multilateral shares assign core contributions to the countries those organisations spend in.
Asia's share of ODA is smaller than it was in 2010.

Country names follow the source's own spelling.
Four of the top five recipients are in conflict.
The Common Framework is the G20's process for restructuring the debt of eligible low-income countries.
The latest year shown is 2023.
Read the bars from left to right: each segment is one sector's share of the total.
New commitments by the World Bank hit USD 128 billion.
The source revises earlier years when donors correct their reports.
Humanitarian aid accounts for one in every seven dollars of ODA.
Switch on "per person" to divide each value by the country's population.
Ghana's debt-to-GDP ratio is above 80%.
